A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same work. Their main text, equations, figures, tables, proofs, and Appendix A are readable and support reliable matching across renumbering and relocation.

before.justification: Section 4 and Appendix A report the authors' parameter estimation from 38 retained Collab-CXR cases. Figures 2–6 also report original numerical analyses of worker behavior and institutional quality.

after.justification: Section 5 and Appendix A retain the original Collab-CXR analysis, while Sections 7–8 add numerical intervention and robustness results.

M1.justification: The baseline model is retained, but v2 adds endogenous institutional transfer optimization, direct verification rewards, quadratic delegation costs permitting interior reliance, and resource-constrained worker choices. These change objectives and feasible procedures, beyond v1's existing extensions.

E1.justification: The radiology dataset, diagnostic task, and clinician example are unchanged. Section 8.2 and Figure 7 add a simulated environment with binding time or cognitive constraints that can make manual execution infeasible. Multi-round interaction and continuous quality are analytical extensions, not additional evaluated datasets.

E2.justification: Manual/no-AI outcomes and the baseline model remain the reference comparisons. The added intervention and workflow variants extend the proposed framework; neither version benchmarks it against additional competing methods.

E3.justification: V2 adds simulation settings for verification rewards, quadratic delegation costs, resource budgets, pessimistic AI beliefs, and nonregular detection/cost functions. The optimized-transfer analysis additionally evaluates Q(Db) + C(Db), rather than institutional quality alone. Existing Collab-CXR filtering, sample size, and exact-match criterion remain unchanged.

E4.justification: Beyond v1's heterogeneous tasks, optimistic beliefs, and partial re-execution analyses, v2 tests whether the conclusions survive interior delegation, resource constraints, pessimistic beliefs, nonconcave detection, and nonconvex verification costs. It also adds optimized-transfer and observable-verification-reward analyses.

E5.justification: Neither version reports repeated-run counts, seeds, confidence intervals, error bars, or significance tests for its original analyses. The additional numerical plots retain the same reporting practice.

E6.justification: New results report smoother transitions under partial delegation, expanded losses under resource constraints, reduced gains and losses under AI underestimation, and reduced degradation under verification rewards. Figure 4c adds gains under an augmented institutional objective. Original Figure 2 results and Collab-CXR success estimates of 0.447, 0.368, and 0.395 are retained.

T1.justification: Sections 8.1 and 8.6–8.8 add formal derivations for interior delegation, multi-round detection, continuous output quality, and relaxed regularity assumptions. Section 7.2 introduces a new institutional optimization problem. The original main theorem proofs remain essentially unchanged.

C1.justification: The abstract and principal introduction/conclusion claims retain the same thesis: incentive misalignment produces workflow thresholds, rational over-delegation, and verification-dependent institutional gains or losses. The expanded analyses primarily support these existing claims.

C2.justification: V2 explains how feasibility constraints can force harmful delegation and why interior reliance can soften transitions without removing incentive misalignment. It adds interpretations of under-reliance and observable verification incentives. Appendix A clarifies which calibration parameters are observed, inferred, or assumed rather than identified.

D1.justification: V2 documents coefficients and functional choices for the new numerical studies and clarifies parameter provenance in Appendix A. Section 6.10 corrects the explanatory scaling constant from 50 to 2; the corresponding detection formula already used 2 in v1. Existing data-processing instructions are retained.

R1.justification: V2 removes the citation to Intelligent AI delegation and its associated reference to task criticality and verifiability. The broader positioning is retained. Publication and bibliographic updates to retained works do not constitute additional cited research.

P1.justification: V2 adds an early interventions/extensions overview, reorders existing extensions, revises explanatory paragraphs, and removes contribution-bullet subheadings. Most original introductory, modeling, theoretical, proof, and concluding text remains substantially intact; much of the expansion is new scientific content.

P2.justification: Figure 1 is redrawn, and v1's combined intervention Figure 3 is separated into worker and institutional displays. V2 adds substantial new panels in Figures 4–8 and 11. Original main-result, heterogeneous-task, and partial-re-execution plots are retained, while Tables 1–2 remain substantively unchanged.

improvement.justification: Broader robustness analyses and clearer parameter provenance improve coverage and interpretation. However, new Section 7.2 maximizes Q(Db) + 0.11Db² over Db ≥ 0 without stating an upper bound. This objective is unbounded as written, leaving Figure 4c's finite equilibrium result unsupported by the stated formulation. The useful additions and this new validity problem prevent a reliable judgment of net improvement.
